Commentary.Commentary: So, that completes our coverage of what was a fascinating Test match. Rain did cause a lot of overs to be lost in each of the first four days but we had enough time to witness a classic Test match albeit at a slow pace at times. So, SL are 1-0 up going to Galle on 4th August. Do join us for that Test match. Until then, it's goodbye from us.

ANGELO MATHEWS is lost for words and expresses his happiness on this big win. Feels that it was a much-needed comeback for the team after the recent disappointments in Tests for the side. Admits that his team batted poorly in the first innings but felt that they had a chance if they could get a lead of above 200. Praises Mendis for his knock while also credits Chandimal for the contributions. Praises Herath for standing up once again and also opines that Sandakan was brilliant. Doesn't feel that captaincy affects his batting and ends by saying that he hopes to contribute in the next match.

STEVEN SMITH feels that it's been a tough week. Credits Sri Lanka for the victory. Opines that they should have got a bigger lead in the first innings but batted poorly. Lauds Mendis for the classy knock and feels that it was difficult to come back after conceding 260-plus. States it was going to be a tough chase and it proved to be so. Accepts that O'Keefe's absence did hurt but doesn't want to point it as an excuse. Ends by saying that Australia need to find out solutions to play spin in the remaining Tests.

KUSAL MENDIS (MAN OF THE MATCH) says that he is very happy with his performance especially as it came in the team's win. Feels that Australia is a very good team and values his efforts a lot. Praises Chandimal for providing support and ends by saying that it was a good win for Sri Lanka.

Australia's bowlers too were guilty of underperforming in the second innings with O'Keefe's hamstring injury also being a reason. Lyon wasn't at his best after a good first innings while Starc was inconsistent. However, credit must go to Mendis for his performance while the Lankan spinners led by the veteran himself - Rangana Herath, spoiled the Australian party. Debutant Sandakan too had a great game as Sri Lanka brought Smith's 11-match unbeaten streak since becoming captain to an end.

The youngster compiled a majestic 176 in a match where only one other batsman got a fifty. His knock along with help from the tail meant that the Lankans had a stiff lead of 267 going into the fourth innings. Chasing that down, particularly on day 4 and 5, is always a very tough ask and the Australians found that out the hard way. The top order was a let down for the tourists and the O'Keefe-Nevill blockathon showed what Australia's batsmen lacked - application.

An incredible comeback by Sri Lanka after having been bundled out for a paltry 117 on the first day and then conceding a lead of 86. The tourists could have got a bigger lead in hindsight but barring Voges, Smith and Marsh, nobody stuck it out there. Still, a lead of 86 was always going to be handy on such a tricky surface but Kusal Mendis' masterclass propelled an unbelievable turnaround to the Test. The Islanders came from behind with a bang through his brilliance.

It seemed like game would be wrapped up quickly but Nevill and O'Keefe pulled the shutters down to forge a very dogged 9th wicket stand that added only 4 runs but ate up 178 deliveries. Sri Lanka were feeling a bit tense mainly due to the weather forecast but de Silva removed Nevill before Herath completed formalities by cleaning up O'Keefe. A thoroughly clinical bowling display by the hosts as they put relentless presure on Australia.

That completes a fantastic win for Sri Lanka as they go 1-0 up in the 3-match series. What a day for the hosts! It's only their second ever Test victory against Australia. Starting the day needing 185 more to win, Australia's batsmen tried hard but couldn't quite survive the trial by spin. Smith conjured a fighting fifty but once he departed, the Lankans took control.

Smith tried his best but got out at the stroke of lunch after his fifty and that was a big blow for Australia. Mitchell Starc didn't trouble the scorers when Sandakan had him caught and bowled. So, Nevill is left to bat with the tail. Let's hope the rain stays away in the second session. Do join us back to catch the action.

Pretty good session for Sri Lanka! They got four big wickets and Australia are reeling at 141/7, needing 127 more runs. Sri Lanka are eyeing their second Test win here in the history against Australia and they're just three wickets away. It was an excellent bowling display by Sri Lanka. The leader of the attack Rangana Herath was at his best once again as he grabbed three wickets in this session. First Voges was out and then after a promising stand Mitchell Marsh got out as well.

The debutant gets the better of Starc and this time he is the one making the long walk back. That will be LUNCH on Day 5.

OUT! Herath gets the early breakthrough! Tossed up ball around off, Voges comes down the track and takes it on the full and pushes it back to the bowler. Herath does well to take a good low catch. He appeals for a caught and bowled and the umpires refer it to the third umpire after having a small discussion. Replays show Voges took it on the full and played it back to the bowler. The ball went off the bat and not off the ground towards Herath. Voges has to go and that's a big wicket for Sri Lanka. Australia are four down and need 172 more runs. Initially the Sri Lankan fielders didn't appeal confidently but after the decision they start celebrating.

Pitch report - There is not much rough on one side and won't turn and bounce much but will skid on. If the batsmen settle in they can score runs. On the other end of the pitch there's a lot of rough and it will keep the batsmen guessing from which part the ball will spin and from where it won't. Patience against the Sri Lankan spinners will be the key for the Aussies to win, reckons Russel Arnold. Ends up by saying that it will be an entertaining day of cricket and will produce a result.
UPDATE 1015 IST - The match will resume at 1045 IST and a minimum of 91 overs to be bowled. First session will be till 1215 IST.
UPDATE 0955 IST - Good news! Covers are coming off and the game might start soon.
Here's the latest tweet by Cricket Australia "Rain slightly heavier now and more covers are out. Frustrating. We'll let you know when a restart is likely."

Welcome! Day 5 is about to begin. Australia have to chase down 185 runs more with 7 wickets in hand. The Sri Lankan spinners will look for some purchase from the pitch and try to bowl out Australia as soon as possible because today's weather forecast also doesn't look good.  As of now the covers have been spread on ground as it rained earlier, so we may have a delayed start.
... Day 5, first session ...

The forecast is not very promising for tomorrow as well. But going by the action so far, even two sessions of play can dish out a result. It's shaping up for a thrilling Day 5. Do join us at 0945 IST for all the action. Cheers!

PLAY HAS BEEN CALLED OFF! Once again, for the fourth day in a row, the third session has suffered. However, this Test match in spite of all the stoppages, is still alive. Australia need 185 runs to win, while Sri Lanka require 7 wickets to go 1-0 up in the series.
Update 1534 IST - It is still very dark out there and there is no play at the moment. Let's hope the heavens stay steady and the clouds clear out soon.

NOT OUT! It's missing leg. Perera hurls in an off-spinner around middle, spinning in a shade to beat the forward defensive prod of Voges. It raps him on the pads, they go up in a huge appeal and umpire Kettleborough raises his finger after thinking for a while. Voges gestures that he is not sure and after having a chat with his skipper, he opts for the DRS. The replays confirm there is no inside edge but the ball is spinning down leg and would have missed the leg stump. Huge reprieve for Voges.
